task.title: Put a formula in your document
task.shortdesc: You write a formula in your XML, or you show a formula from a file. Then you choose its font, its size and its color, and you decide whether it sits in a line of text or on a line of its own.

step.cmd: Write the formula in your XML

info.p: Add a math element in the MathML namespace where the formula must appear. CSSMedia draws it on the line of the text that surrounds it, and the baseline of the formula is the baseline of the line:

You can declare the namespace with a prefix instead, as in <m:math xmlns:m="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">, and write m:mi, m:mo and so on. A math element in another namespace is an ordinary element of your XML, and CSSMedia does not draw it as a formula.

step.cmd: Choose a line of text or a line of its own

info.p: A formula is inline by default: it is part of a line, and its parts are compact so that the line stays even. Set display="block" on the math element to put the formula on a line of its own. A block formula is in display style: fractions, limits and big operators take more room and get their full size. Compare the same fraction in both styles:

stepxmp.p: In a line of text, the fraction is one over one plus x, small. With display="block" it is on a line of its own and has its full size:

image.alt: One over one plus x, in full size.

info.p: The attribute displaystyle of mstyle changes the style for the elements it holds. Style a formula explains it.

step.cmd: Or show a formula from a file

info.p: A file with one math element is an image. Make an element of your XML show it with content, as for any other image. This stylesheet shows the file named by the src attribute of a formula element, inline:

The file is a document of its own. The style sheets of your document do not reach into it, so the file names its own style sheet with an xml-stylesheet instruction, and that sheet declares the font. A file without such an instruction has no style sheet:

image.alt: x equals minus b plus or minus the square root of b squared minus four a c, over two a.

info.p: A file is drawn at its natural size, and the width and height of the element scale it with everything in it, glyphs included. An inline formula sits on the baseline of its line.
Declare a font with a MATH table in your style sheet and set it for the math element. The rule needs the MathML namespace, so declare it first with @namespace:

With a font that has no MATH table, CSSMedia uses the fallback values of MathML Core for the bar of a fraction, the height of scripts and the like. Operators keep their normal glyphs, and nothing stretches.
An mi element that holds one letter is drawn in the mathematical italic style, as MathML asks for. Write mathvariant="normal" on the element to get an upright letter.

step.cmd: Set the size and the color

info.p: The font-size of the math element is the size of the text in the formula, and color is its color. Scripts, such as the exponent in x², are smaller than the text, as Style a formula explains:

step.cmd: Link a part of the formula

info.p: An a element with an href attribute makes the formula inside it a link, and so does any other MathML element that has an href:
